Sector Trend & Position-Sizing Study

Golden/death-cross behaviour across 11 sectors built from 5,179 symbols, combined with a macro market-health score to size a long/short trend strategy — designed to go both ways and lean on the market's overall health.

Prices are monthly; the 3m/10m cross is the monthly analogue of the 50-day/200-day golden & death cross. Universe is survivorship-biased (only symbols still present), so absolute index levels and buy-&-hold returns overstate reality; the trend/whipsaw structure and relative comparisons are the signal.

2 · How often crosses are fake breakouts

A cross is flagged a fake breakout / whipsaw if it reverses within 4 months or never travels a 5% favourable move before the opposite cross. This is the core risk of naive crossover trading — and it varies a lot by sector.

3 · How far price stretches from trend

How far the index deviates from its 10-month MA before reverting. Wider bands (Technology, Consumer Cyclical) mean bigger overshoots — more room for stop placement and mean-reversion, but also more violent reversals.

4 · Do the crosses actually pay?

Average forward 12-month return after each golden vs. death cross. Positive golden-cross bars mean the signal has historically led real trends in that sector.

6 · Which sectors feel macro-regime shifts most

Forward 12-month sector returns conditioned on the macro regime (the latent financial-conditions regimes from the Dalio model — no sector prices in the features, so no circularity). The right-hand bars rank sectors by their best-minus-worst-regime swing: high-beta cyclicals (Health Care, Consumer Cyclical) swing most between regimes; defensives (Energy) least. These are the sectors to lever into on a favourable regime shift and to hedge first on an adverse one.

7 · Market health for position sizing

The health score blends trend breadth (share of sectors above their 10m MA) with financial conditions (NFCI, high-yield spreads, VIX, the yield curve) and broad momentum, all as causal rolling z-scores. Above 50 = risk-on (size longs up); below 50 = defensive (scale down, allow shorts). It reads 87 today.

8 · The strategy: cross + health-sized sizing

Five books, monthly rebalanced, one-month signal lag (no look-ahead), equal risk across sectors. Fair accounting: idle cash earns the risk-free rate, trades cost 10 bps of turnover, and shorts pay a 100 bps/yr borrow fee.

  • Buy & hold — always long every sector.
  • Cross long-only — long a sector only while its 3m>10m (golden regime).
  • Cross long/short — long in golden regime, short in death regime, full size.
  • Health-sized long/short — long size = health, short size = (1−health): full shorts only when the market is weak.
  • Health-scaled long-biased — stay long the trend but sized by health (de-risk in stress); add shorts only when health < 35.

Read the honest result: over a 25-year bull, the trend filter's main gift is drawdown control — long-only cuts max drawdown roughly in half versus buy-&-hold at a similar hit rate. Naive shorting drags returns; health-sizing's value is that it only lets you short when the market is genuinely weak, and de-risks longs into stress. Both directions are available, but the data says: be long-biased and let market health govern how much.

9 · Leverage & hedging with carry cost

The real payoff of a regime filter is that it lets you use leverage without getting wiped out. Four books on the broad market — static 1×/3×/5× and a regime-timed ladder — one-month lag, with realistic carry: borrowed capital pays the risk-free rate + 50 bps, shorts pay a 100 bps/yr borrow fee, and each exposure change costs 10 bps. The regime-timed book runs 3× when health ≥ 75, 2× ≥ 60, 1× ≥ 45, ½× ≥ 30, and −1× (hedge short) below 30.

1x buy & hold-57.5078.30-0.64-100.0036.00
Static 3x (carry-adj)-100.00234.70-0.66-100.0036.00
Static 5x (carry-adj)-100.00391.20-0.67-100.0036.00
Regime-timed 1–3x + hedge-100.00124.90-0.32-100.0039.00

Static high leverage is a ruin machine: the 3× book draws down -100%, and the 5× book hits a >100% monthly loss and the account goes to zero — permanent ruin, no recovery possible. The regime-timed 1–3× book targets the levered upside but cuts exposure (and flips to a hedge) when health rolls over, so its drawdown stays survivable — which is the only way leverage compounds. Carry is a real drag (≈0.5–1.5% a year when levered/short) and is already deducted here. Monthly rebalancing is generous to the static books: intra-month margin calls and daily-reset decay are not modelled, so real 3×/5× products are strictly worse than shown.

Method & caveats

  • Monthly data. The dataset has no per-symbol daily prices, so the 50/200-day cross is implemented as a 3m/10m monthly cross (Faber-style). Change with --fast/--slow.
  • Survivorship. Only currently-present symbols exist, inflating levels and buy-&-hold. Relative/behavioural results (whipsaw rates, deviation, drawdown control) are far more robust.
  • Point-in-time cap weights. Sector indices weight month t's returns by market cap at t−1 (price at t−1 × latest share counts — no historical share data), so no future prices leak into the weights. Symbols without share data get the cross-sectional median cap. Still broad proxies, not investable indices.
  • Costs modelled. Idle cash earns rf; trades cost 10 bps; shorts pay 100 bps/yr borrow; leverage pays rf + 50 bps financing. Real leveraged-ETF path decay (daily reset) is not modelled — monthly rebalancing understates the drag of daily 3× products.
